valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E, with the forward period viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) taken as FY2028 non-GAAP diluted EPS. Anchor: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $24.45-$24.50 (raised with Q3 results, about 400M diluted shares, about 45% non-GAAP operating margin); Street FY2027 EPS about $27.43. Scenario FY2028 EPS is my own assumption: bear $25.50 (growth stalls, AI disruption of seat-based creative software), base $28.50, bull $31.00 (buybacks plus AI-first ARR growth). Per share of the USD Nasdaq listing; no ADR or FX conversion applies.

bear.driver: Revenue growth fades and AI-native competitors compress pricing, so the market keeps a trough multiple

base.driver: Revenue grows about 10-11% as guided (Q3 revenue $6.76B, +13%), margin holds near 45%, buybacks offset dilution

bull.driver: AI-first ARR (up 150%) scales, new CEO from 1 Dec keeps margins and the multiple re-rates toward large-cap software

valuation.implied_by_close: At FY2026 guided EPS of about $24.48 the close of $243.08 implies 9.9x; at base FY2028 EPS of $28.50 it implies 8.5x. The Oct-Nov named targets average about $229 (range $200-$267), which is 8.0x base FY2028 EPS, or EPS of $24.1 at 9.5x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $28.50 (10.5% of the $271 base, 11.7% of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Total Adobe ARR growth and non-GAAP operating margin against the 44% Q4 guide, plus FY2027 EPS guidance versus the Street $27.43.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance, expected in December 2026.

analyst_notes: Named-firm targets reset lower in Oct-Nov 2026: Goldman $200 (Sell), Wells Fargo $225 from $270 (downgrade to Sell), HSBC $267 from $310 (downgrade to Hold), TD Cowen $245 and Citi $207 from $250. Only Goldman's analyst (Gabriela Borges) is named in found sources; others are labeled by firm and none has a documented 12-month horizon, so none enters the weighted target. These targets sit about 15% below the base case, equivalent to base EPS near $24 at 9.5x rather than $28.50; the gap is mainly a multiple and growth-durability disagreement. The sample is thin and partly from an aggregator.
